title: Three-step LLM integration quickmap (draft)
content:
Purpose
A tiny, executable roadmap for an engineer to go from zero to a running, observable LLM feature in ~3 hours. Target audience: product/engineer pairing building a first POC or a small iteration for an existing app.

Goals
- Make a safe, repeatable 3-step path that minimizes cognitive overhead.
- Surface the smallest set of guardrails and telemetry needed to call something "production-friendly" for early rollouts.
- Provide copy-paste snippets and a checklist for handoff to SRE or product infra.

Constraints / Assumptions
- Customer uses Redwood hosted API for initial POC. Private/Dedicated notes are in "Next actions".
- Language model calls are stateless (no long-term KV caching) for the first iteration.
- App has an existing backend service (Node/Python) where an SDK can be added.

Three steps (summary)
1) Scaffold: add SDK and a minimal request path.
2) Guard: add timeouts, retries, and input validation.
3) Observe & iterate: wire telemetry, a tiny eval set, and rollout rules.

Step 1 — Scaffold (30–60m)
Objective: wire a single end-to-end path from UI to model and back.
Minimum deliverables:
- Add Redwood SDK to backend (npm/pip).
- Implement one route /api/compose that proxies user text to Redwood and returns safe-processed output.
- Add simple client-side UX: a text input, loading state, and error fallback.

Notes / copy-paste (Node.js example)
- npm install @redwood/inference
- const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference');
- const r = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
- // minimum call
- const resp = await r.generate({ model: 'rw-base-1', prompt: userText, maxTokens: 150 });
- return { text: sanitize(resp.text) };

Sanitization: strip control chars, enforce length cap, map any null/undefined to empty string. Avoid complex safety filters in the first pass — surface candidate failures in logs for review.

Step 2 — Guard (30–45m)
Objective: ensure the integration behaves predictably and degrades gracefully.
Checklist:
- Request timeout: 1.5–2x target UI latency. (e.g., 3s target → 4.5–6s timeout)
- Circuit breaker: open after 5 consecutive errors for 30s
- Retries: 1 retry with exponential backoff for 5xx/timeout only
- Input size limits: reject inputs > 8k chars with a helpful client message
- Output length cap: truncate outputs > 2k tokens and surface truncated flag to client

Example policies (pseudocode)
- fetchWithPolicy(req) {
-   return retry(fetch, { retries: 1, onRetry: incMetric('redwood.retry') })
-     .withTimeout(6000)
-     .catch(err => { incMetric('redwood.error', err.type); throw err; });
- }

Step 3 — Observe & iterate (45–90m)
Objective: gather signals to decide whether to promote the feature or rollback.
Minimum telemetry to ship:
- Per-request latency histogram (p50/p95/p99)
- Token usage per request (tokens_in, tokens_out)
- Success/error rate and error classification (4xx vs 5xx vs safety-filter)
- User-level feature adoption (DAU for feature) and per-session failure rate
- Outcome quality probes: a tiny eval set (10–20 prompts) run nightly, compare embedding similarity or heuristic scoring vs baseline

Implementation tips:
- Tag metrics with route, model, customer_tier (internal), and env (staging/prod)
- Use a sampling policy for traces (1% full traces, 100% error traces)
- Expose a simple dashboard: "LLM > compose" with latency, errors, and tokens; link raw logs for failed request ids

Quick eval harness (recommended)
- Add a cron job to run the eval set against the live model variant and push results to the dashboard. Alert if score drop > 5% vs baseline.

Rollout pattern (safe default)
- Start internal-only for 24–48h (team + 5% beta users)
- Monitor quality/economics for that window; if metrics pass, expand to 25% then 100% with 24h between steps
- If errors or eval regressions occur, automatic rollback to previous stable model (or stub fallback)

Handoff checklist for SRE / infra
- Config: model id, max concurrency, timeout, retry/circuit settings
- Cost cap: set daily token budget alert
- Audit: list of linked dashboards and alert playbooks
- Compliance: confirm logging doesn't contain PII (redact if necessary)

Safety & privacy quick notes
- Do not log full user inputs by default. Use hashed IDs + noise for debugging.
- If customers supply PII-sensitive prompts, route to a private deployment plan (see "Next actions").

Open questions / engineering decisions
- Do we want to provide a client-side SDK helper for optimistic UI updates? (pro: smoother UX; con: complexity for cancellation / cost accounting)
- Should we ship an out-of-the-box small eval runner in the SDK or keep it in infra tooling?

Next actions (owner / timeline)
- Today (Avery): implement Scaffold route + basic telemetry (2–3h)
- +2d (Samir): add guard policies, circuit breaker tests, and chaos injection tests (2–4h)
- +5d (Lina): implement nightly eval runner + dashboard and run internal canary (4–8h)
- Product: draft UX copy for failures and truncated responses

Appendix — Danger signals (kill switch triggers)
- p95 latency > 3x baseline for 1h
- Daily token cost > 2x forecast for 24h without matching adoption growth
- Eval score drop > 5% or large unexplained semantic drift in outputs

Notes to self
- Keep this doc intentionally small; we should link to longer patterns once we stabilize. Prioritize reproducible examples and a single Node and Python snippet for the public quickstart.

Version history
- 2024-11-05 created by Avery Chen
- 2024-11-21 updated: added telemetry sampling guidance (Samir)
summary: Short executable three-step guide to ship a minimal, observable LLM feature using the Redwood SDK. Focus on scaffold -> guard -> observe.
